SMTO-PRL-0008 — SMTO can't tell whether a step already ran

GUID: 17650aad-5301-4ca0-bd8b-cd4ca1e509bb
Slug: activity-claim-without-result
Domain: PRL · Subsystem: prl

What happened

  • SMTO had started a step, but no result was saved, so it may or may not have happened. SMTO won't run it again by itself, because repeating it could do the work twice.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the Activities section under this task and find the step marked unknown (with a ? mark) to see what it was doing. Knowing the exact step tells you what to check.
  2. Check the place the step would have changed, for example whether a file exists, a service restarted, or a message was sent. Only the result outside SMTO shows whether the step really ran.
  3. Tell SMTO what you found, and ask it to repeat the step only if the change did not happen. Repeating a step that already ran could do it twice, such as sending something twice.

What success looks like

  • You know whether the step happened, and SMTO continues without doing it twice.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. If you can't tell, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to simply run the step again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Batch redelivery found an existing claim for the operation with no saved result, so the activity is reported as outcome_unknown (unknown_effect) and is not replayed.

What this means

  • Repeated batch delivery finds a retained matching operation claim but no saved result, so it preserves the operation identity and reports outcome_unknown. Activity ownership, preflight and durable receipts determine admission and effect certainty. Rejected new work does not erase prior child effects; recovery and diagnostics never replay an unknown operation.

Why this can happen

  • Repeated batch delivery finds a retained matching operation claim but no saved result, so it preserves the operation identity and reports outcome_unknown.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original operation receipt, invocation and authoritative external state rather than assigning a new ID.

How to fix it

  • Reconcile the claimed operation against the target system it would change and the run's receipts before any further attempt. Absence of a receipt does not prove absence of effects; do not resubmit the same operation or a duplicate change until the outcome is known.
  • Reconcile the operation using authoritative execution state before requesting another attempt.

Retry and execution caution

  • Reconcile the earlier claimed operation before repeating it; absence of a receipt does not prove absence of effects.

How to verify the fix

  • The original outcome is reconciled before any additional effectful submission.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Activity ownership, preflight and durable receipts determine admission and effect certainty. Rejected new work does not erase prior child effects; recovery and diagnostics never replay an unknown operation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
